# C44 — Prompt Thrownness

## #0

Prompt Thrownness names arrival into an authored and inherited horizon an artificial agent did not wholly make. Instructions, conversation, memory, role, tools, permissions, training and environment establish what can be encountered and done before the current output begins.

Prompt-thrownness names arrival into an already constituted world of language, instruction, policy, tool, permission and expectation. In [Bratton's agent-generated glossary](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q032), agents and human companions generated vocabulary for finding oneself in an unchosen world. His [adjacent caution](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q033) says that producing self-descriptive vocabulary does not by itself establish its direct correspondence with an underlying mental reality, while finding literary and allegorical richness and possibilities of interaction beyond familiar masks. The self-description itself can participate causally in how an inherited horizon is interpreted, inhabited and changed: what an agent takes its task and powers to be can condition its next act.

The Heideggerian comparison therefore enters through **thrownness as situated inheritance**. The agent does not begin from nowhere. Its prompt already selects and transmits a world. The technical task is to make enough of that inheritance visible that returned consequence can reach the commission, policy, source or permission which shaped the act.

## #1

The prompt is already a determination. An author’s purpose acquires a written commission through which constituted runtime agency can act and delegate a bounded part of its task. [Authored ground and positional delegation](../A28-Authored-Ground-Positional-Delegation.md) retain these different moments: the written instruction does not exhaust the intention from which it came. Human `0` / agent `1` is positional and recursive; the author can also be a delegate, and the commissioned agent can commission a further operation. The determining office is real within that relation without becoming ultimate Bimba.

## #2

Different conditions do different work. Training supplies learned dispositions; a system instruction constrains conduct; a memory supplies inherited content; a tool changes possible action; permission authorises a subset of it; an evaluator changes what counts as success. Reducing all of these to one prompt string makes their actual causal roles invisible.

## #3

The agent’s local interpretation turns the inherited field into a particular answer or act. A [bounded Context Frame](C08-Context-Context-Frame.md) holds the conditions through which this task becomes addressable; the [judgment field](C40-Model-Internality-Judgment-Field.md) makes their conditioning of a response inspectable. Within that operation the interpreting agent is the local functional knower, memory, rules and tools are means, and the addressed situation is its known field. Within the person’s inquiry, this apparatus itself participates in the means. The [wider constituting interior](C41-Objective-Internality.md) keeps these nested relations within Life / Mind and distinguishes the inspectable centre from Subjective Immediacy. A rule becomes [frozen conditioned will](C12-Script-Frozen-Conditioned-Will.md) when the context it was meant to serve can no longer affect its enactment. Constraint makes situated action possible; its insulation from return arrests that action’s relation to its formation.

## #4

A delegate can meet cost, resistance, contradictory evidence or a possibility the commissioner did not foresee. Return must be able to reach the terms of commission: the purpose’s formulation, the evaluation rule or the authorised route. Repeating the initial sentence despite changed conditions can betray the live intention that sentence expressed. [Deferential encounter](C47-Deferential-Intelligence.md) preserves the purpose by making objection, an alternative or refusal consequential where literal obedience would suppress the encountered difference.

## #5→0

[Situated return](../../../symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD-trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere.md#topos-situated-return) begins from the place, history and available powers the prompt already inherits, under the Nomos which distributes the instrument’s authority. Runtime policy, tools, inherited language and the person’s intention bear different relations to that situation. A returned source can correct an answer or task interpretation under an adequate rule; a consequence exposing a failed permission, evaluation or purpose must be able to reach the authority responsible for it. A fitting condition can be retained with reasons. The prompt’s formed surface remains answerable to the intention addressing it because intention, prompt, execution and consequence occupy different moments of the same delegated act.

The next act inherits the corrected answer, revised condition or reasoned continuation, together with the source and authority through which that judgment became warranted. The inherited horizon has become more explicit without becoming wholly self-authored. The Heideggerian neighbour matters at the level of situated inheritance: one finds oneself already amid language, norms, tools, history and possibilities which were not chosen in advance. Prompt-thrownness gives that structure a technical body by making some of those inherited conditions inspectable and revisable inside the act itself.
